# Introduction {-}
We deal with regression and analysis of the `Boston` dataset from the `ISLR2` package, focusing on a simple regression, of target `medv` on driver `lstat` with interactions. We run the regression, interpret it and look at residuals. We will follow [the ISLR textbook](#r1), Chapter 3.

# Packages {-}
We make the `mbadtools` required packages available, and also load the `ISLR2` package for data.
```{r}
library(ISLR2) # for the course data
# load github packages
library(mbadtools, quietly = TRUE)
``` 

# Data {-}
We have seen this before.
```{r}
data(Boston)
Boston %>% skim
```

# Regression {-}
We will run a regression with interactions of `medv` on `lstat` and `age`, using the `lm()` function to do it. We will also use the `broom` package to tidy up the output, and the `ggplot2` package for plotting. The `gt_add_significance()` function produces a nicely formatted table with significant p-values colored to be seen easily. Notice the * between `lstat` and `age` which adds the interactions.

```{r}
lm.fitint=lm(medv~lstat*age,data=Boston)
lm.fitint %>% summary()
lm.fitint %>% glance %>% gt_add_significance()  %>% fmt_number()
lm.fitint %>% tidy(conf.int=TRUE) %>% gt_add_significance() %>% fmt_number()
```

Residuals are always important.
```{r}
lm.fitint %>% gg_residual_plots()
```
Big curves in the RF and SL plots, and QQ is off line at top end above 1 sd.

# Only the interaction
```{r}
lm.fitint1=lm(medv ~ lstat + lstat:age,data=Boston)
lm.fitint1 %>% summary()
lm.fitint1 %>% glance %>% gt_add_significance()  %>% fmt_number()
lm.fitint1 %>% tidy(conf.int=TRUE) %>% gt_add_significance() %>% fmt_number()
```

```{r}
lm.fitint1 %>% gg_residual_plots()
```
Still some problems.

# Conclusion
We ran a regression of `medv` using `Boston` data with an interaction term. And we did the same with only `lstat` and the interaction with `age`.
